newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. urged to halt hotel sales by Turkish Cypriots.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urged to halt hotel sales by Turkish Cypriots.

text.p: Cyprus has asked the United Nations to prevent the Turkish Cypriot authorities from selling two hotels in the north of the island that it said were owned by Greek Cypriots.

In a letter to Secretary-General Kofi Annan circulated on Tuesday, Cypriot U.N. envoy Nicos Agathocleous said the "illegal secessionist entity set up in the occupied areas of Cyprus" had announced it intended to put up the two hotels for sale.

They were The Dome hotel in Kyrenia and The Salamis Bay hotel in Famagusta, "which were illegally usurped from their rightful owners following the Turkish invasion and occupation of a large part of Cyprus in 1974," the letter said.

Turkish troops landed in northern Cyprus in 1974 after a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece. In 1983, the Turkish Cypriots proclaimed their own state that is recognised only by Turkey.

Agathocleous said selling the hotels was intended as "first steps in a so-called privatisation programme." But such properties belonged to "their legal owners who were forcibly uprooted from their ancestral homes and properties by the Turkish invading and ocupying forces," he added.

He cited a decision by the European Court of Human Rights in a property case last December which he said concluded that the applicant remained "legal owner of her property in the occupied area and that Turkey was in violation of the European Human Rights Convention by preventing her from returning to and enjoying her property in Kyrenia."

Referring to the planned sale of the two hotels, Agathocleous said: "On behalf of the government of the Republic of Cyprus, I strongly protest these illegal Turkish actions and request the immediate intervention of the United Nations to prevent them from taking place."

He told Annan that "these Turkish actions take place at a most sensistive phase of the Cyprus problem, at the very time when you are exerting determined efforts to bring about a just and lasting solution."

Annan plans to open talks next month between the leaders of the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities aimed at reuniting the island under a federal system -- a goal that has eluded the United Nations for more than two decades.
